manifest.name: @equalang/dsh-plugin
manifest.description: Equalang for DeepSeek Harness: translate documents, slides, spreadsheets, e-books, subtitles, pictures, audio and video with their layout kept, and transcribe recordings.
manifest.author: Equalang

bundle.text:
# The layer DeepSeek Harness applies when a profile lists this bundle: one row,
# which mounts the Equalang MCP server through dsh's own MCP client.
#
# Settings go on this row's `config` in the profile's cordis.patch.yml, or, for
# the key, on the plugin's page under Plugins:
#
#   - id: equalang
#     config:
#       apiKey: el_...
- insert:
    - id: equalang
      name: '@equalang/dsh-plugin'

readme.text: **Translate the file, keep the layout — inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).** This plugin gives the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) agent the tools of [Equalang](https://equalang.com), an AI translator that works on whole files: a PDF comes back as a PDF, a deck as a deck, with tables, images and formulas where they were. It also translates subtitles and pictures, turns audio and video into translated subtitles or a transcript, and translates text in bulk.

The tools are the ones the [Equalang MCP server](https://github.com/equalang/equalang-mcp) offers every other agent. The plugin starts that server with DeepSeek Harness's own runtime, so it works in the desktop app with no Node.js installed, and hands it your key.

- "Translate ~/Documents/contract.pdf into Chinese, keeping the layout."
- "Translate pitch-deck.pptx into Japanese and German."
- "How much would it cost to translate thesis.docx into French?"
- "Make Korean subtitles for interview.mp4, with the original line above each one."
- "Transcribe standup.m4a with timestamps."

In the DeepSeek Harness desktop app or web UI, open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter

```
@equalang/dsh-plugin
```

and choose **Install**, then **Enable now**.

From a terminal, for `dsh web`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @equalang/dsh-plugin
```

then restart `dsh web`. Use the profile name you start dsh with; the desktop app keeps its own profile, so install there through its **Plugins** page.
Needs DeepSeek Harness 0.2. The desktop app brings everything else; the `dsh` command needs Node.js 24.9 or later, as dsh itself does.

Sign up at <https://equalang.com> and create a key at <https://equalang.com/api-keys>. New accounts start with free credits, enough to put a document through.

The simplest place for it is `~/.config/equalang/.env`, the one file every Equalang integration reads, so a key saved once for Claude Code, Codex or the Equalang skill works here too:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/equalang && echo 'EQUALANG_API_KEY=el_your_key' > ~/.config/equalang/.env && chmod 600 ~/.config/equalang/.env
```

The plugin looks in two places before that file, so a key there wins:

1. **The plugin's own setting**, `apiKey` on the `equalang` row of your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` (the profile is `web` for `dsh web` and `desktop` for the desktop app), or `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` for every profile. Add the row to the list the file already holds:

```yaml
   - id: equalang
     config:
       apiKey: el_your_key
   ```

2. **`EQUALANG_API_KEY` wherever DeepSeek Harness looks for keys**: its credential store, the environment dsh was started from, or `~/.dsh/.env`.

DeepSeek Harness does not pass exported variables whose names look like credentials to the MCP servers it starts, so the plugin hands the key over itself. A changed key takes effect without restarting DeepSeek Harness.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp__equalang__translate_file` | Translate a document, subtitle file, picture or recording, and save the result beside it |
| `mcp__equalang__transcribe_recording` | Write down what a recording says, as timed text |
| `mcp__equalang__translate_text` | Translate strings, or one long text |
| `mcp__equalang__estimate_cost` | Upload a file and say the most a job on it can cost, without starting anything (free) |
| `mcp__equalang__check_job` | Collect a job that was still running when its call returned |
| `mcp__equalang__cancel_job` | Stop a job; a cancelled job costs nothing |
| `mcp__equalang__get_credit_balance` | The account's credits |
| `mcp__equalang__list_languages` | The language codes Equalang takes |

Files are named by an absolute path or a public URL, and results are written beside the source without overwriting anything. A long file can take minutes: a call waits up to 50 seconds by default, then answers with a job id for `check_job`.

- Jobs spend your Equalang credits, the same balance as on the website. `estimate_cost` is free. DeepSeek Harness runs MCP tools without asking you first, so the agreement comes from the model: the server tells it to say the cost and get your agreement before a job. Credits are bought at <https://equalang.com/pricing>. The model the agent runs on is billed separately, by DeepSeek or whichever provider you chose.
- A file you ask to translate is uploaded to Equalang to be processed. See the [privacy policy](https://equalang.com/legal/privacy).
- Like every MCP server DeepSeek Harness starts, this one runs outside the agent's sandbox: it reads the file you name and writes its results beside it under any permission preset.

On the `equalang` row of a profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, as shown above for the key. A change applies without a restart.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apiKey` | none | Your Equalang API key |
| `baseUrl` | `https://equalang.com/v1` | Another deployment of the Equalang API |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `600000` | How long one tool call may run before DeepSeek Harness gives up on it |

- **No Equalang tools.** Check that the plugin is enabled under **Plugins**, and restart after installing from a terminal. DeepSeek Harness refuses to install or start a plugin made for another version of itself, and says which version it needs.
- **`EQUALANG_API_KEY is not set`.** Save the key in one of the places above. An `export` in your shell alone does not reach the server.
- **Installed from a terminal, missing in the desktop app.** `dsh plugin --profile web` installs into the `web` profile; the desktop app uses its own. Install through the app's **Plugins** page.

- [equalang-mcp](https://github.com/equalang/equalang-mcp), the MCP server this plugin runs, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients.
- [equalang-skill](https://github.com/equalang/equalang-skill), the same operations as an Agent Skill. DeepSeek Harness also loads skills from `~/.agents/skills`.
- The Equalang API: <https://equalang.com/llms.txt>
